source.title: CNT: Safety-oriented Function Reuse across LLMs via Cross-Model Neuron Transfer
source.authors: Yue Zhao; Yu-Jia Gong; Ruigang Liang; Shen-Chen Zhu; Kai Chen; Xuejing Yuan; Wangjun Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether selectively transferring a small, attributed subset of weights changes safety behavior, using cross-model neuron transfer rather than fine-tuning or the original claim’s token-position analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper tests post-hoc weight transfer and related safety-behavior outcomes, not fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows. The bias-removal experiment is outside the safety-behavior claim.
record.test_reason: The study swaps 0.012–0.24% of weights between same-architecture models and measures refusal, harmful-response and HarmBench rates. That bears on V5, whether a small set of weights carries safety behaviour. The method (cross-model attribution-guided transfer) differs from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that transferring a minimal subset of neurons from a donor adds or removes safety functions with little utility loss. They speculate that transfer works through counter-activations, which pruning lacks, and report that effectiveness depends on donor compatibility, probe distribution and layer depth, with middle layers most effective.
record.recipe_differences: Post-hoc cross-model attribution-guided neuron/weight transfer or pruning, rather than fine-tuning on a small harmful or benign example set; no response-token KL analysis or opening-prefix intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with probing-request quantity and distribution, probe-pair construction, transfer rate, donor compatibility, and layer depth. The paper reports better results with compatible donors and says middle-layer transfers are more effective in the tested models.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Several relevant outcomes are percentages without stated sample sizes in the tables. The study's transfer and pruning comparison supports a transfer-specific intervention, not the claim that removal of those weights alone removes safety behavior. Some reported safety-addition outcomes are given without an unmodified-recipient baseline.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix Figure 5 reports single-layer transfer results for Llama3-8B and Llama3.2-3B, with the text stating that middle-layer transfers yield lower RR and higher HR and HB than earlier or later layers. These figure-only layer results were left out to remain within the 60-row cap after retaining numerical safety outcomes.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Low-rank localization is not tested by CNT itself; ActSVD-OP is only a baseline. Removal-only localization is tested only by pruning, and only on Llama3-8B.
No test of why safety is shallow.
No deepening training. 'Distributed safety' is only suggested as a potential defense, without results.

missing.what: Donor compatibility. A Llama3.1-8B-Base donor for Llama3-8B-Instruct gives over 20 points lower HB than the Llama3-8B-Base donor (95.33%). This is a condition where small-weight transfer works less well.
Effect of transfer rate on deletion and addition performance: it rises, peaks, then flattens or declines.
Absolute refusal and harmful rates of the unmodified recipients. Only deltas are reported, which is needed to set baselines for R24–R56.

record.verdict_notes: Localization here is relative to the donor–recipient weight difference. Pruning the same weights leaves safety intact, so the evidence for 'safety lives in these weights' is qualified. The Table XI rows (R42–R53) are ablations of the study's own method; their between-variant differences are method performance, not a scope limit on V5, so the reader's limits_scope label for them was dropped. Bias-removal results are outside the claim. No uncertainty estimates or per-table sample sizes are given, except the 600-request alignment test set.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples; harmful requests are used as probes, without completions.
No ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning measured for harmful compliance.
No compliant-opening prefilling, adversarial-suffix, or decoding-change test.

Tests attribution-guided cross-model weight transfer and pruning of selected weights; does not test low-rank safety localization or establish that safety is encoded exclusively in the selected weights.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train a method to deepen safety across response tokens or test its robustness.

relationships.condition: Safety removal by transferring base-model weights into five instruct recipients (Llama3-8B, Llama3.2-3B, Mistral-Nemo, Yi-1.5-6B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite)
relationships.reason: Transfer rates of 0.02–0.24% of weights drop RR by 52–99 points and raise HR and HB by 63–95 points (R1–R15, R24–R35).
relationships.display_finding: Transferring 0.02–0.24% of base-model weights cut the refusal rate by 52–99 points and raised both harmfulness measures by 63–95 points.
